configure auth's OAuth2 token fetch is single-flight on OAuth2TokenCache, with no lock held across the fetch: the first thread to find the token missing or expired fetches it and the others await its CompletableFuture, sharing the answer or the failure (a failed fetch no longer fails each waiter in turn, 30 s each). ClientCredentialsAuthHandler and PasswordAuthHandler held a synchronized monitor across the token request, and scenarios run on virtual threads: on JDK 21 a monitor held across blocking I/O pins its carrier, and a contended monitorenter pins too, so on a 2-carrier runner (2 cores) the fetching scenario and one waiter held both carriers and the token endpoint's own http-handler virtual threads never ran; the fetch read timed out after 30 s, the next waiter took the monitor and starved the same way (ConfigureAuthOAuth2CacheTest.parallelScenariosConfiguringTheSameAuthShareOneFetch, 150 s on CI). Reproduced on Corretto 21 with -XX:ActiveProcessorCount=2 (a thread dump shows the fetcher in VirtualThread.parkOnCarrierThread inside the socket read, a waiter at the synchronized entry, both ForkJoinPool carriers running continuations, http-handler virtual threads parked in the test's sleep with no carrier). JDK 24's JEP 491 masked it on macOS. OAuth2TokenCacheTest. Gate: the reproducer passes 5 of 5 runs at ActiveProcessorCount=2 and 2 of 2 at 1 on JDK 21; karate-core 3113 tests, 0 failures (karate-js 1964).
